resources.string: Vazie VPN has a Quick Settings tile: one tap to open or close the tunnel, without opening the app.
How to add it by hand
Pull the quick settings panel all the way down.
Find Vazie VPN among the tiles that are not in use.
Drag it up into the active tiles.
Holding the Vazie VPN icon offers your saved configurations directly. Nothing to set up — they are already there.
Hold the Vazie VPN icon on your home screen.
Let go on the configuration you want.
Vazie VPN on your home screen
Two widgets: Quick Connect, which is one button, and a Dashboard with the session read-out. The button below asks your launcher for Quick Connect — add the Dashboard from the widget list.
How to add one by hand
Hold an empty spot on your home screen.
Find Vazie VPN. There are two.
Choose a size and drag it out.
For the Dashboard, find it in the same list and drag that one out too.
Changes the icon on your home screen. Your configurations and any live connection are untouched; some launchers take a moment to catch up.
If your phone recolours icons to match its theme (themed icons), Monochrome or Pearl on the Light background will look best.
What Vazie VPN stores, where, and what it never collects.
\@vazieapp — news, releases and questions about the app
Vazie VPN is made by one person, in the evenings and at weekends. Helping is entirely optional and unlocks nothing — there is nothing to unlock. The app is free and always will be.
Vazie VPN is made by Vazovsky
One person, evenings and weekends. Personal contacts here; questions about the app go to Vazie and support below.
Here is exactly what Vazie VPN holds, where it holds it, and what it never sees.
Your configurations: the server address, the port, the transport and security settings, and the keys needed to connect.
Your choices: which configuration is selected, the theme, the app icon, and which tips you have dismissed.
When each configuration was last used successfully — a timestamp, and nothing about what went through it.
Configurations and their keys are encrypted on this device, with a key held by Android\'s keystore. They are not readable by other apps and are not copied anywhere.

Your theme, icon and dismissed tips are in a plain file — they are preferences, not secrets, and keeping them out of the encrypted store means a display setting cannot break the store that holds your keys.
Nothing is included in Android\'s cloud backup. A restored phone starts with no configurations rather than with keys that travelled through somebody else\'s storage.
No behaviour analytics, no advertising identifiers, no location. Vazie VPN sends no crash reports.
No account, no email, no phone number, no device identifier: Vazie VPN never asks who you are.
No browsing history, no visited addresses, no record of what you connected to or when, beyond the last-used timestamp above.
Vazie VPN writes to the Android log only in debug builds, and never writes a key, a UUID, a share link or a server address into it. A release build is quiet.

While connected, your traffic goes through the server in the configuration you chose. That server can see the destinations your device asks for, exactly as your network provider could otherwise. Vazie VPN is the client; it does not run in between.
DNS queries follow the tunnel while it is up, so they go to the same server rather than to your provider.
A configuration you imported is yours. It stays on this device, is never uploaded and costs nothing.

A home-screen widget shows the selected configuration\'s name, its protocol and the session\'s duration and traffic. Those are stored in the widget\'s own preferences so it can draw itself while Vazie VPN is closed — on this device, and never a key or an address.

Long-pressing the icon offers up to three configurations by name. A name that looks like an address, a link, an e-mail, an IP or a UUID is left out rather than shortened: a launcher label is visible without unlocking anything.
The quick-settings tile shows the connection state and nothing else. It never names a configuration.

Export produces the original share link, and that link contains the credentials that connect to the server. Anyone who receives it can use the server as you. Vazie VPN hands it to Android\'s share sheet at the moment you ask and keeps no copy.
How to set up and use Vazie VPN
How to get started, and what each of the parts of Vazie VPN that live outside the app is.
While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN can sit in your status bar with a Disconnect button on it — so you can stop it without opening the app. Notifications are off right now, so it can\'t.
While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN sits in your status bar with a Disconnect button on it, so you can stop it without opening the app.
Open your phone\'s settings, then Apps.
Find Vazie VPN and open its notifications.
Turn on the VPN connection notification.
A quick walk through the main screen.
What a configuration is and where to get one.
To use your own VPN, Vazie VPN needs a configuration — a link with the settings for a server. You usually get one from a VPN provider, from whoever runs the server, or from a server you run yourself.
It is normal for it to look like a long line of strange characters. Paste it into Vazie VPN and it will read the details for you.
An example of a configuration link
%1$s. If Vazie VPN doesn\'t recognise a link, it will say so and won\'t try to guess.
Open or close the tunnel without opening Vazie VPN.
Hold the icon and pick one — nothing to set up.
Quick Connect and a Dashboard, on your home screen.
The tunnel in your status bar, with a Disconnect button.
Once you have a configuration, everything you can do with it is in two places: the list, and the configuration\'s own screen.
Tap a configuration to use it. Swipe it to delete it — deleting always asks first.
Open a configuration to rename it, duplicate it, or export it. Duplicating makes a second copy on this device; deleting removes it from this device only.
Export creates a shareable configuration. It can contain the credentials needed to connect, so treat it like a password.
